physical_skill: Seat a PH2 screwdriver held level in a 6 mm recess on a hinge arm inside an open wall cabinet, push it in with at least 10 N while keeping it within 6 degrees of the screw's axis, and turn it clockwise against 0.2 N m by 0.5 to 1.1 turns (more than one wrist twist, so easing off and winding back with the tip still seated), then shut the door so the gap to the next door reads 2-3 mm and even at both ends.
valid_shortcuts: None that score full: doing nothing 0; turning with the tip seated but without pushing 0; pushing and turning with the gripper 20 degrees off axis 0 (10 degrees off lets the driver pivot back to ~4.5 degrees in the grip and turns 0.28 turn: 0.25); turning the right screw the wrong way 0; over-turning 1.75 turns 0.25; turning correctly but leaving the door open 0.25; holding the shut door 0.5. Turning the top hinge's screw instead cannot reach the 1.0 window by geometry. One arm could in principle shut the door too; the task does not claim two-handedness.
distinct_from_nearest: The only board task with this exact operation is the lapsed #3101 (claimed here after its hold). Against #1865 (flap door, custom hinge) and accepted screwdriving tasks, the distinct ability is adjusting an installed hinge to a measured target by a seated, pushed, aligned screwdriver in a confined installed cabinet. Residual risk: importance is judged afresh (#2407 was closed for good on importance for hinge reattachment), so the README argues the jobs case with BLS and O*NET sources and labels the inference.
